title: The parameter version event has no place in the rwb-case event catalogue
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-042 section 12 (ParameterVersionApproved); context pack ownership rows for P3 rwb-case (events EV-01 to EV-05, EV-19, EV-29); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-09 and DP-14
section: s12.3 Events published; s12.4 Events consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story publishes ParameterVersionApproved to refresh every parameter cache, and the preserved criteria AC1, AC8 and AC11 depend on a refresh without a restart. The Ownership Map gives rwb-case seven event rows (EV-01 to EV-05, EV-19, EV-29) and none of them is a parameter event: no EV number is allocated, the catalogue gives no key and no payload field list beyond the three values the legacy section 12 names (paramKeys, versionNo, validFrom), and the module technical specification carries no entry for it either. The topic and the CloudEvents envelope are fixed by DP-09 and DP-14, but without a catalogue row the event cannot be declared as a contract element with a settled name, key and payload.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-042 section 12: 'Publishes ParameterVersionApproved (new internal event, see additions: paramKeys, versionNo, validFrom) to the outbox; every instance refreshes its cache'; the P3 ownership rows list EV-01 to EV-05, EV-19 and EV-29 only; TSD P3 v3 gives no parameter event.
proposed: Add the parameter event to the rwb-case event catalogue with its number, key and payload, or rule that the cache time to live is the only refresh; until then publish rwb.case.ParameterVersionApproved.v1 on rwb.case.events.v1 with the payload of the assumption and keep the time to live as the fallback.

title: The run-time read of the catalog by the other 18 services has no published operation, right or key artefact
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-042 section 4 step 2 and section 12 (published ParameterService interface); Technical Specification P3 v3 API-P3-018; Ownership Map row GET /admin/parameters; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-06 and DP-11
section: s3 Preconditions; s11 Data; s12.1 REST operations provided; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s13 Solution plan
description: In the monolith every caller of a parameter was in the same JVM and read ParameterService with a generated key. After the split the only published read of the surface is GET /admin/parameters, whose right in the technical specification is Rules and parameters R with scope applied, an administration right held by a person. No source gives the operation, the right, the scope or the keys artefact another service uses at start-up and at run time, and the request the platform client of RWB-PLT-E1042-CON makes is not stated, so AC4 (a service does not start without a required value) and AC3 (the completeness check compares the keys a service reads) cannot be settled from the sources. The columns of a load row beyond key, environment and value are also unnamed.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-042 section 12: 'public interface ParameterService { <T> ParameterValue<T> get(ParameterKey<T> key, LocalDate businessDate); }' with 'P3, package recovery.casewf.config.api (published)'; TSD P3 v3 API-P3-018 GET /admin/parameters, Authorization 'Rules and parameters, right R, scope applied'; no service-to-service read appears in the ownership rows.
legacy_ref: RWB-E1-042 (AC3, AC4, AC8, section 4 step 2, section 12)
proposed: Add the run-time read of the catalog to the Ownership Map with the right a service identity holds, and record the keys artefact the platform client publishes; until then serve the key-prefix query of GET /admin/parameters to a service identity holding Rules and parameters R, as the assumption states.

title: The target form of the names, migration numbers and catalog key that survived the monolith is not restated
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-042 sections 3, 7, 8, 12 and 13; Technical Specification P3 v3 T3 (parameter_catalog id and param_key); Template and Rules R4 and R5.5 DP-15
section: s3 Preconditions; s7 Acceptance criteria (AC2, AC3); s12.7 Tables owned; s13 Solution plan
description: Five legacy names are fixed by the as-built copy and have no target form in any source: the Java package the two build checks scan (recovery.casewf.config, and recovery.casewf.casecreation in the section 7 background and in AC2), the used_by value the catalog carries for each parameter, the feature flag rwb.p3.configservice (the default ruling puts feature flags in the platform library, which allocates no name), the file numbers the two migrations take in the per-service sequence (the as-built copy carries V042_1 and V042_2 of the single recovery schema), and the primary key of parameter_catalog, which the as-built migration puts on param_key while the logical model also carries id as DF-REF-132. None of the five is a business value, and all five have to be fixed before the app story can run its build checks and its migration.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-042 section 13: 'Package. recovery/casewf/config (Java package recovery.casewf.config)'; 'Feature flag. rwb.p3.configservice'; 'V042_1__parameter_catalog.sql' and 'V042_2__parameter_seed.sql'; section 7 background and AC2 name 'recovery.casewf.casecreation'; TSD P3 v3 T3 gives parameter_catalog id DF-REF-132 and param_key DF-REF-133 and no primary key.
proposed: Fix the five names in the rwb-case repository and the service template: the target package, a used_by convention, the flag name the platform library allocates, the next free numbers of the rwb-case sequence, and one primary key for parameter_catalog.

title: The rights of the four operations are not republished under the rwb-case ownership
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-042 sections 5, 10 and 12; Technical Specification P3 v3 API-P3-018; Ownership Map (reference-load paths owner P3); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-08
section: s3 Preconditions; s10 Authority; s12.1 REST operations provided; s14 Validation and messages
description: The legacy rights are Reference data C for a load, Reference data U for a rollback, Reference data A for an approval and Rules and parameters R for the read, and the reference-load paths moved from rwb-access to rwb-case. The technical specification still gives GET /admin/parameters only the Rules and parameters R right, and no source states which capability area and which right the three write operations carry now that rwb-case owns them, nor whether a service identity may hold one. The refusal is fixed (403 with MSG-P4-002) but the grant is not, so the contract cannot publish a complete rights matrix from the sources.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-042 section 12: 'Authorization | Reference data, right C' on the load and 'Reference data A' on the approve; TSD P3 v3 API-P3-018: 'Rules and parameters, right R, scope applied'; no right row appears for the reference-load paths in the technical specification.
proposed: Confirm the capability area and the right of the three write operations with the rwb-access owner and record them in the authorise model; until then the contract keeps the legacy rights and resolves them through the guard the service template wires.
